rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a training supplementary, a lookup surface under §9's reference/supplementary waiver. Chunk 1 (TL;DR) bolds the four composition-mechanism names in one paragraph -- fits 'a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' (four named mechanisms, four handles). Chunk 2's axis table and Layer-3 mechanism list ('1. Explicit load.' etc, 2-4 words each) and chunk 4's workflow-table row labels ('A · Standard feature', etc) are table/menu row-labels, each an independently ≤5-word handle. Chunk 5 (Design principles) bolds a full lead sentence (5-8 words) per numbered paragraph entry followed by explanatory prose -- matches §9's own carve-out 'on a prose-paragraph lookup page, the bolded lead sentence IS the handle' for entries that are 'paragraphs rather than label+prose rows'; bold never crosses the first-sentence boundary in any of the 7 entries. Chunk 6's 'Marker legend' + three `[R]`/`[C]`/`[O]` marker bolds are a legend/glossary row-label pattern, same menu waiver. Chunk 7 bullets are short lookup-row leads (3-5 words). Chunk 0's lede line 5, '**Read for the patterns, not for copying.**' (7 words), is the one bold that does NOT fit a waiver -- it is narrative preamble, and §9 states explicitly that 'a reference page's narrative preamble is still narrative,' so the lookup-surface carve-out does not reach it. Weighed against the rule's actual harm (bold fatigue / diluted signal from an over-used emphasis channel): this is the file's only narrative-preamble bold, one span in a 168-line body, immediately followed by unbolded prose for the rest of the lede -- it functions as the page's single opening thesis-emphasis, not a pattern of overused bold, so the harm the budget guards against is not present. Filed as a suggestion below rather than a REVISE.
